Simp
SIMP
noun / verb (Gen-Z slang)
Clipped from simpleton, which American English had shortened to simp by the early 1900s (a fool, a sap). The modern sense — a man who over-does attention, money, or flattery toward a woman in hope of her favour — grew in 1980s–90s hip-hop (Too Short’s lyrics are the usual citation), then exploded on TikTok and Twitch in 2019–2020, where "simping" meant tipping a female streamer or gushing in her comments. A crude acronym later attached to it online is a backronym, not the source; the word is a century older than the acronym.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang a simp is a young man who makes himself small for a woman’s attention: he over-texts, over-tips, over-praises, and treats her approval as the prize of his life. Boys use it to mock any visible kindness to a girl ("holding the door? simp"), which is the word’s first lie. The Christian observation cuts both ways. There is a real sin the word half-sees: a man whose heart is turned by a woman until he forgets his God. Solomon’s "wives turned away his heart after other gods" (1Ki 11:4), and the young man void of understanding is led "with the flattering of her lips" (Pro 7:21). That is idolatry wearing a lovesick face, and "the fear of man bringeth a snare" (Pro 29:25). But the slang throws out the gold with the dross. It teaches boys that tenderness is weakness and that the only safe posture toward a woman is cool detachment. Scripture commands the opposite of both errors: "Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it" (Eph 5:25). Christ is no simp — He does not beg for the church’s approval — and He is not aloof; He lays down His life. A father tells his son: you will not grovel for any girl’s favour, because you already have your Father’s; and you will not be ashamed to serve a woman, because that is what your Lord did for His bride.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z slang (from 1900s simp, simpleton; 1990s hip-hop; TikTok/Twitch 2019–present) for a man who grovels for a woman’s attention — a real idolatry the word half-sees, and a sneer at chivalry the word wrongly teaches.

SIMP, n. (Gen-Z slang, c. 2019–present; earlier hip-hop) A man who over-does attention, money, or flattery toward a woman in hope of her favour. "He paid for her whole order and she left him on read. Simp."

SIMP, v.i. To act as a simp; to fawn. "Stop simping in her comments." Simping, n., the behaviour.

Used loosely, and wrongly, of any courtesy a boy shows a girl — opening a door, paying for dinner, defending her.

Webster (1828), root word simpleton: “SIM'PLETON, noun A silly person; a person of weak intellect; a trifler; a foolish person.”

Decode for parents: your son is being taught that kindness to a girl is humiliation; your daughter is being taught that a man’s devotion is something to farm.

Key Scripture

1Ki 11:4 — "For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father."

Pro 7:21 — "With her much fair speech she caused him to yield, with the flattering of her lips she forced him."

Pro 29:25 — "The fear of man bringeth a snare: but whoso putteth his trust in the LORD shall be safe."

Eph 5:25 — "Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it;"

Gal 1:10 — "For do I now persuade men, or God? or do I seek to please men? for if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ."

Modern Corruption

Simp names a real idolatry — a man whose heart is turned by a woman’s approval — and then misuses the name to shame every act of tenderness, leaving boys with cold detachment as the only safe manhood.

expand to see more

The word sees one true thing. A man can make a woman’s favour his god, and Scripture has a long list of them: Samson undone on Delilah’s lap, Solomon’s heart turned by his wives (1Ki 11:4), the young man of Proverbs 7 led "as an ox goeth to the slaughter." That is not romance; it is the fear of man in its most flattering form, and it is a snare (Pro 29:25). A boy who tips a streamer his lunch money to be noticed has a worship problem, not a dating problem.

But the slang turns the diagnosis into a weapon against virtue. It teaches boys that courtesy is humiliation and that the only safe posture toward a woman is the sneer. Christ answers both sins at once. He is not the man begging for approval — "if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ" (Gal 1:10) — and He is not the man too cool to serve; He "loved the church, and gave himself for it" (Eph 5:25). Teach your son that difference: secure in the Father’s favour, and therefore free to lay down his life for a wife without asking hers first.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Simpleton → early-1900s American simp (a fool) → 1990s hip-hop: a man who fawns over women → 2019–2020 TikTok / Twitch: simp, simping.

expand to see more

Latin simplex — single, plain; English simple, simpleton (a silly person)

Early 20th c. American slang: simp, a fool or sap

1980s–90s hip-hop: simp for a man who fawns over women

2019–2020 Twitch and TikTok: tipping or gushing at female creators called "simping"

Now a playground insult for any boy who is kind to a girl
